title: Audit event contract, storage, and migration guidelines for RBAC v2 and SSO
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Define a stable, compact audit event contract and taxonomy to support RBAC v2, SSO/SAML identity mapping, and admin controls; specify diff encoding for object changes; and provide storage, indexing, and migration guidance to enable low-latency queries, SIEM ingestion, and compliance retention. This ticket covers schema fields, redaction rules, event typing, and operational constraints (size limits, backfill plan). Not covered: auditing UI experience (separate DES/PM tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Audit event contract doc exists and is approved by Security and Compliance
Canonical field set includes actor, actor_identity_source, target, action, outcome, pre/post diffs (compact format), request_id, timestamp, and context metadata
Diff format chosen (compact key-diff) with examples and encoder/decoder reference implementation link
Storage and indexing guidance provided with recommended retention buckets (30d/365d/7y) and redaction rules
Migration plan for historical events defined with estimated runbook and low-impact rollout steps
Integration guidance for SSO/SAML mapping and RBAC v2 attributes included
proposed_schema: Top-level stable fields: event_type, timestamp (RFC3339), request_id (opaque), actor (principal string), actor_identity_source (sso|saml|oidc|internal), actor_id_hash (sha256-redacted) optional, target (resource canonical string), action (verb), outcome (success|failure|warning), diff (compact key-diff string), context (semi-structured; key=value;max 512 chars), severity, region, service, schema_version. Field length limits and requiredness are documented.
diff_encoding_choice: Compact key-diff (textual delta tokens) chosen for smallest event size and human readability. Encoder produces tokens like +path[value] -path[old]. We will standardize escaping for arrays and maps. Reference encoder in PR #3248.
storage_retention: Recommend three retention tiers: hot(30d, indexed for console/SIEM), warm(365d, cheaper storage with secondary indices for compliance queries), cold(7y, compressed blobs for legal). PII redacted in hot tier; retained as hashed-only in warm/cold unless legal exception.
indexing_plan: Index on (timestamp, event_type, actor_id_hash, target, request_id) in hot tier. Provide columnar export to warehouse daily for analyst queries. Add dedicated mapping for SIEM ingestion (CEF/LEEF) in separate exporter service.
privacy_risks: Direct email addresses in actor/target could leak PII — must apply redaction policy for first-class outputs
Context fields may contain secrets (tokens) — enforce max length and regex-based redaction for known secret patterns
SAML assertions included raw in logs are forbidden; only subject id and identity_source allowed
migration_plan: 1) Add schema_version to new events and start dual-writing (old contract + new contract) for 2 weeks. 2) Backfill critical indices by replaying compressed events through a transform job that emits new schema into hot index. 3) Run validation queries and compare counts. 4) Switch consumers to new topic and retire old contract after 30d. 5) Archive legacy events to cold storage once validated. Estimated infra cost: ~1200 compute-hours for backfill.
rollout_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased event size causing log throughput spikes — Mitigation: enforce 8KB per-event cap; trim context and require diff compaction
Risk: Downstream consumers break on new fields — Mitigation: use schema_versioning and dual-write; provide compatibility shim in eventbus
Risk: Latency on hot indexing — Mitigation: rate limit backfill and use async bulk APIs
